timeline.current_model: ACSL4 is a long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase with substrate preference for polyunsaturated fatty acids (especially arachidonic and adrenic acids) that acts as a critical pro-ferroptotic enzyme by esterifying PUFAs into membrane phospholipids, providing the peroxidation substrates required for ferroptosis execution; its activity and stability are tightly regulated by multiple post-translational modifications—including phosphorylation by PKCβII (activating) and CDK1 (triggering UBR5-mediated ubiquitin degradation), SUMOylation by TRIM28 at K532 (stabilizing), acetylation by HAT1 at K383 (stabilizing, blocking FBXO10-mediated degradation), lactylation at K412, m6A-dependent mRNA stabilization via METTL3/YTHDC1, and autophagic degradation via HSC70/CMA or OPTN-selective autophagy—while its transcription is driven by SP1, Sp1, STAT1/IRF1, STAT3, E2F (downstream of RB1), EGR1 (downstream of YAP), and NFIL3, and inhibited by HIF-1α; beyond ferroptosis, ACSL4 promotes tumor metastasis by remodeling membrane phospholipid composition to activate integrin β1 signaling and enhance membrane fluidity, reprograms lipid metabolism through the c-Myc/SREBP1 axis and FAO-dependent histone acetylation, regulates neuroinflammation via VGLL4/NF-κB, and interacts directly with partner proteins including STING, FUNDC1, and MMD/MBOAT7 to modulate disease-specific lipid peroxidation pathways.
